paragraphs.en: The train door opened, and the smell hit me before my feet touched the platform. Salt, wet wood, and something sweet from the kiosk. Eight years, and Harrow Bay still smelled exactly the same.
paragraphs.zh: 车门打开，还没等下到站台，那股气味就扑面而来。咸味、湿木头味，还有小卖亭飘来的甜味。八年了，哈罗湾的气味一点没变。

paragraphs.en:
"You're standing in the doorway," said a voice behind me.

"I'm having a moment," I said.

"Have it on the platform."
paragraphs.zh:
“你堵在门口了。”身后有人说。

“我在感受这一刻。”我说。

“去站台上感受。”

paragraphs.en: I stepped out. The station was small, as I remembered. One line along the sea, a wooden roof, a bench with peeling paint. I had a suitcase, a school bag, and no clear plan for the year. I wanted quiet. I wanted to keep my head down and finish second year without any turbulence.
paragraphs.zh: 我走出去。车站很小，和我记忆中一样。沿海一条线，木屋顶，一张掉漆的长椅。我拎着行李箱、背着书包，对这一年没什么明确计划。我想要安静，想低着头、平平稳稳地念完二年级，不要有任何波折。

paragraphs.en: The kiosk beside the ticket gate was still there. It was a small wooden stand with a glass case of snacks, a shelf of maps, and a hand-written sign that said OPEN. Behind it sat a girl in a Northlight High uniform, drawing in a sketchbook. She did not look up.
paragraphs.zh: 检票口旁的小卖亭还在。那是个木头小摊，玻璃柜里放着零食，架子上摆着地图，还有一块手写的牌子，写着“营业”。亭子后面坐着一个穿北光高中校服的女孩，正在速写本上画画。她没抬头。

paragraphs.en:
"Excuse me," I said. "Is the bus stop still on the left?"

"Right," she said, still drawing.

I looked right. There was the bus stop.

"Thanks."

"Mm."
paragraphs.zh:
“打扰一下，”我说，“公交站还在左边吗？”

“右边。”她说，还在画。

我往右看。公交站就在那儿。

“谢谢。”

“嗯。”

paragraphs.en: The bus climbed the slope toward school, and I pressed my forehead to the window. Lantern Street passed below, shutters half open, a bakery with a warm light in its window. My heart did something awkward and sudden, and I looked away.
paragraphs.zh: 公交车沿着斜坡往学校开，我把额头贴在车窗上。灯笼街从下面经过，卷帘门半开着，有家面包店的窗里透出暖光。我的心突然别扭地跳了一下，我移开了视线。

paragraphs.en: The first day of second year is always a mess. New class lists, new seats, new rules nobody explains. I found Class 2-B on the second floor and walked in. A boy with a wide grin grabbed my shoulder before I even sat down.
paragraphs.zh: 二年级的第一天总是乱糟糟的。新的分班名单、新的座位、没人解释的新规矩。我在二楼找到2-B班，走了进去。我还没坐下，一个咧嘴笑的大个子男孩就一把抓住了我的肩膀。

paragraphs.en: "New guy!" he said. "Park. Theo Park. I know everything about this town and nothing about you, which is a problem I plan to fix." He talked like a congress of one, all motion and no pause. "You came from the city? Big city? Did it have, like, real buildings?"
paragraphs.zh: “新来的！”他说，“帕克。西奥·帕克。这镇上的事我全知道，你的事我一点不知道，我打算解决这个问题。”他说话像一个人开的议会，一刻不停。 “你从城里来的？大城市？有真正的高楼吗？”

paragraphs.en:
"It had buildings," I said. "Some of them were big."

Theo nodded with great seriousness. "I can work with that."
paragraphs.zh:
“有楼，”我说，“有的还挺高。”

西奥一脸严肃地点点头。“行，这个信息有用。”

paragraphs.en: Ms. Hale read the class list in a flat voice and assigned committee work to anyone who sighed too loudly. She also asked for a student to help the council sort old files after school. Nobody raised a hand. Then the door opened and someone answered for me.
paragraphs.zh: 黑尔老师用平板的声音念分班名单，谁叹气太大声就派谁去做委员会的工作。她还问有谁愿意放学后帮学生会整理旧文件。没人举手。这时门开了，有人替我回答了。

paragraphs.en:
"Elliot Reed will do it," said a girl with dark hair and a perfect ribbon. She said my name like she had checked it against a list. "He needs to learn the school. I'll supervise."

"I don't remember agreeing," I said.

"You hesitated," she said. "That's close enough."
paragraphs.zh:
“埃利奥特·里德会去。”一个深色头发、系着完美丝带的女孩说。她说我名字的样子，像刚从名单上核对过。“他需要熟悉学校。我来监督。”

“我不记得自己答应过。”我说。

“你犹豫了，”她说，“差不多了。”

paragraphs.en: Her name was Vivian Ashe. Student council secretary, top of the year, and clearly someone who enjoyed watching people tangle themselves up in their own words. I could tell she had a strong sense of her own prominence, and a weakness for using it.
paragraphs.zh: 她叫薇薇安·阿什。学生会书记，年级第一，显然还喜欢看别人被自己的话绕进去。我看得出她对自己挺有优越感，也爱把这份优越感拿出来用。

paragraphs.en: After the last bell, I went to the council office. Vivian handed me a box of old papers without a word. Sorting them was boring, but the window was open and the sea was right there, so I didn't mind.
paragraphs.zh: 最后一节课的铃响后，我去了学生会办公室。薇薇安一句话不说，递给我一箱旧文件。整理这些很无聊，但窗户开着，海就在眼前，我倒不介意。

paragraphs.en:
On my way out, an old woman stopped me near the library. She was small and bent, and she held a brown parcel with both hands. "You're the Reed boy," she said. "You have your mother's eyes. This was left for you. It says to give it to you when you come back."

"When I come back?" I said. "I only moved away."

She just smiled and put it in my hands.
paragraphs.zh:
出来的时候，一位老太太在图书馆附近叫住我。她个子矮小，背有点弯，双手捧着一个棕色包裹。“你是里德家的男孩，”她说，“你有你妈妈的眼睛。这是留给你的。上头写着等你回来的时候交给你。”

“等我回来？”我说，“我只是搬走了而已。”

她只是笑了笑，把包裹放进我手里。

paragraphs.en: Inside was a small leather notebook. It was water-stained and soft at the corners, palm-sized, and clearly old. Inside the cover someone had drawn a map of the town by hand. I opened the first page at the bus stop.
paragraphs.zh: 里面是一个小小的皮面笔记本。水渍斑斑，边角都软了，巴掌大小，显然很旧。封皮内侧有人手绘了一张镇子的地图。我在公交站翻开第一页。

paragraphs.en:
The handwriting was childish and neat. Seven pages. Seven promises. The first one said: I promise to eat Nora's cooking for a week and say it is good every single time. — E.

I turned the page. The seventh page was sealed with old tape, and written on the front in a voice I could almost hear: To the girl who waited at the station.
paragraphs.zh:
字迹幼稚却工整。七页纸，七个约定。第一个写着：我承诺吃诺拉做的饭整整一星期，而且每次都说好吃。——E。

我翻到下一页。第七页用旧胶带封着，封面上写着一句我仿佛能听见的话：给在车站等的那个人。

paragraphs.en: Nora. The bakery on Lantern Street. The girl in my old class who once pushed me into the sea and then cried about it. I sat on the bench and read the page again, letters wavering and people moving around me, and for the first time in eight years I felt something I could not put into a well-labeled genre.
paragraphs.zh: 诺拉。灯笼街那家面包店。我旧班上的那个女孩，曾经把我推进海里，然后又为此哭了。我坐在长椅上又读了一遍那页，字迹在眼前晃动，周围有人在走动。八年来第一次，我感到一种我说不清、归不了类的情绪。

paragraphs.en:
The bench creaked. Someone sat down beside me, very close, and then a hot paper bag was put into my hands.

"You're back," Nora said. "You're really back. I didn't believe it when the bakery got the delivery address. Eat. You look like a weed that survived winter."
paragraphs.zh:
长椅吱呀一声。有人在我旁边坐下，靠得很近，然后把一个热乎乎的纸袋塞进我手里。

“你回来了。”诺拉说，“你真的回来了。面包店收到送货地址时我还不信。吃。你看起来像一棵熬过冬天的杂草。”

paragraphs.en: She was loud. Even her silence was loud. Her name was written clearly on the first page of the notebook, and she was watching me open the bag with the defense of someone who had rehearsed this and was still scared.
paragraphs.zh: 她声音很大。连沉默都很大声。笔记本第一页上清清楚楚写着她的名字，而她看我打开纸袋时，那副样子像是在防守，像一个排练过很多遍却仍然很紧张的人。

paragraphs.en:
"Nora," I said. "Do you remember a notebook? A promise notebook?"

Her face went through several expressions quickly, then settled on a wide, determined grin. "Nope," she said, in the voice of a person who absolutely did.
paragraphs.zh:
“诺拉，”我说，“你记得一个笔记本吗？一个写约定的笔记本？”

她脸上飞快地闪过好几种表情，最后定格成一个大大的、坚决的笑容。“不记得。”她说，用的却是那种“绝对记得”的语气。

paragraphs.en:
"You're a terrible liar."

"I'm a great liar," she said. "You just have a chronic habit of seeing through me. Eat the bread, El."
paragraphs.zh:
“你撒谎撒得很糟。”

“我撒谎撒得很好，”她说，“你只是有看穿我的老毛病。吃面包吧，埃尔。”

paragraphs.en: I ate the bread. It was good, because it came from her parents, not from her. I appraised the notebook again while she watched me from the corner of her eye. Then she took the last bun, gave it to me, and ran for the train she did not need to catch.
paragraphs.zh: 我吃了面包。面包很好吃，因为她父母做的，不是她做的。她斜着眼看我的时候，我又仔细看了看那个笔记本。然后她拿走最后一个面包，塞给我，然后跑去赶那趟她根本不用赶的火车。

paragraphs.en: On the ride home, a sea wind came through the window and rumpled the pages. I turned them over and counted: one, two, three, four, five, six. And a sealed seventh. Under the map inside the cover, there was one more line, small and pressed into the paper: We don't break these. We don't forget.
paragraphs.zh: 回家的车上，海风从窗里灌进来，把书页吹得翻动。我把它们翻过来数：一、二、三、四、五、六。还有一个封着的第七页。封皮内侧的地图下面，还有一行小字，压进了纸里：这些我们不撕毁，也不忘记。

paragraphs.en: The bus turned along the seawall. The old Annex building stood dark behind the school, and its clock had stopped at 4:10. I had seen it a hundred times as a child. That night it looked like a question someone had left for me, and I had just promised myself a quiet year.
paragraphs.zh: 公交车沿着海堤转弯。学校后面，旧别馆黑沉沉地立着，上面的钟停在4:10。小时候我见过它一百次。那晚它看起来像有人留给我的一道问题，而我刚刚还对自己保证要过安静的一年。

paragraphs.en:
At home, my sister Iris was waiting at the door. She is fourteen, sharp, and keeps a notebook of her own, though hers is called a suspicious behavior log and I am the main entry.

"You're late," she said. "What's in the bag?"

"Homework," I said.

"Homework doesn't have a ribbon."
paragraphs.zh:
回到家，妹妹艾里斯在门口等着。她十四岁，很精明，也有一个笔记本，不过她那本叫“可疑行为记录”，而我常常是主要条目。

“你回来晚了。”她说，“袋子里是什么？”

“作业。”我说。

“作业不会系丝带。”

paragraphs.en: I hid the notebook under a book on my desk. Before bed I opened the seventh page one last time under my lamp. The tape was old. The paper underneath was too new, and the handwriting was not quite mine. I turned off the light and stared at the dark ceiling, and the small voices inside me would not settle.
paragraphs.zh: 我把笔记本藏在桌上的书下面。睡前，我在台灯下最后看了一次第七页。胶带很旧，可下面的纸太新了，笔迹也不太像我的。我关了灯，盯着黑黑的天花板，心里的那些小声音怎么也平静不下来。

paragraphs.en: My phone lit up. An unknown number. One line: You opened it, didn't you. I'll tell you the rules tomorrow. Don't do anything stupid before then.
paragraphs.zh: 手机亮了。一个陌生号码。只有一行字：你翻开了，对吧。明天我告诉你规则。在那之前别干傻事。

paragraphs.en: I lay there in the dark, and outside, a train passed along the sea and did not stop.
paragraphs.zh: 我躺在黑暗里。外面，一列火车沿着海开过去，没有停。

paragraphs.en: The next morning, Nora was waiting outside my house with a lunchbox and a smile that was too bright for seven in the morning.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天早上，诺拉带着一个便当盒和灿烂得不像早上七点的笑容，在我家门外等着。

paragraphs.en: "You're late," she said. "The rules meeting started five minutes ago."
paragraphs.zh: "你迟到了,"她说,"规则会议五分钟前就开始了。"

paragraphs.en: I blinked at her. "What rules meeting?"
paragraphs.zh: 我眨了眨眼。"什么规则会议?"

paragraphs.en: She pushed the lunchbox into my hands. "The notebook rules. Mia sent a message to the group chat. Vivian added a document. Theo added eleven stickers. It's a congress."
paragraphs.zh: 她把便当盒塞进我手里。"笔记本的规则。米娅在群聊里发了消息。薇薇安加了一份文档。西奥加了十一个表情贴纸。简直是个议会。"

paragraphs.en: I opened the lunchbox. Inside was a piece of toast with a face drawn on it in jam. The face was screaming.
paragraphs.zh: 我打开便当盒。里面是一片吐司，上面用果酱画了一张脸。那张脸在尖叫。

paragraphs.en: "That's my first attempt at cooking," Nora said proudly. "It's a precaution. In case you try to run."
paragraphs.zh: "那是我第一次尝试做饭,"诺拉自豪地说,"这是预防措施。以防你逃跑。"

paragraphs.en: I ate the toast. It was dry and the jam was too salty. I tried not to let my face show anything, but Nora was already watching me like a scientist appraising a failed experiment.
paragraphs.zh: 我吃了吐司。面包很干，果酱太咸。我努力不让表情透露什么，但诺拉已经像科学家评估失败实验一样看着我了。

paragraphs.en: "It's... wholesome," I said.
paragraphs.zh: "很...健康,"我说。

paragraphs.en: "Liar," she said, but she was smiling. "Come on. We need to coordinate before school. Vivian is already talking about regulatory approval."
paragraphs.zh: "骗子,"她说，但她在笑,"来吧。上学前我们需要协调一下。薇薇安已经在说监管批准了。"

paragraphs.en: We walked to school together, and I learned the rules of the notebook the hard way: Nora explained them while also trying to steal the notebook from my bag.
paragraphs.zh: 我们一起走去学校，我以艰难的方式学到了笔记本的规则：诺拉一边解释，一边试图从我包里偷走笔记本。

paragraphs.en: "Rule one," she said, grabbing for my bag. "A promise must be kept as written. No substitutes."
paragraphs.zh: "规则一,"她说着，伸手抓我的包,"承诺必须按写的履行。不能替代。"

paragraphs.en: I held the bag away from her. "And rule two?"
paragraphs.zh: 我把包拿开。"那规则二呢?"

paragraphs.en: "A promise is kept only when the other person says so. So I have to say you did it. And I will say so when you have eaten my cooking for a week and praised it."
paragraphs.zh: "承诺只有在对方说完成时才算完成。所以我得说你也做了。等你吃了我做的一周饭菜并赞美它，我就会说。"

paragraphs.en: The word "praise" hung in the air with a lot of prominence. I had a feeling my praise would be tested.
paragraphs.zh: "赞美"这个词在空中格外突出。我有种预感，我的赞美会受到考验。

paragraphs.en: At school, the situation was already tangled. Vivian was waiting at the gate with a printed copy of the school charter. Theo was next to her, holding a bag of chips and looking delighted.
paragraphs.zh: 在学校，情况已经纠缠不清。薇薇安拿着一份打印的学校章程等在门口。西奥在她旁边，拿着一袋薯片，看起来很高兴。

paragraphs.en: "The notebook is a historical document," Vivian said. "It should be part of the centennial exhibit. I have checked the regulatory requirements for school displays."
paragraphs.zh: "笔记本是一份历史文件,"薇薇安说,"它应该成为百年纪念展览的一部分。我已经检查了学校展览的监管要求。"

paragraphs.en: Nora stepped forward. "It's not a document. It's a promise. And promises are private."
paragraphs.zh: 诺拉走上前。"它不是文件。它是承诺。承诺是私密的。"

paragraphs.en: Vivian adjusted her glasses. "Then perhaps we can render a compromise. The notebook stays with Elliot, but I supervise. To prevent any turbulence in the promise-keeping process."
paragraphs.zh: 薇薇安扶了扶眼镜。"那么也许我们可以达成一个妥协。笔记本留在埃利奥特那里，但我监督。以防止承诺履行过程中的任何动荡。"

paragraphs.en: I looked at Theo. "Why are you here?"
paragraphs.zh: 我看着西奥。"你为什么在这里?"

paragraphs.en: "I'm the comic relief," he said. "Also, I started a betting pool. Current odds are Nora three to one, Vivian five to one, Mia ten to one."
paragraphs.zh: "我是喜剧调剂,"他说,"另外，我开了个赌局。目前赔率是诺拉三比一，薇薇安五比一，米娅十比一。"

paragraphs.en: Mia appeared behind him without a sound. She was holding a sketchbook and looked at me with her usual deadpan expression. "Ten to one?" she said. "That's low."
paragraphs.zh: 米娅悄无声息地出现在他身后。她拿着速写本，用一贯的面无表情看着我。"十比一?"她说,"太低了。"

paragraphs.en: The bell rang. We had to go to class, but the argument followed us like a chronic headache. In homeroom, Ms. Hale assigned me to the centennial committee as a punishment for "excessive social prominence." I hadn't said a word.
paragraphs.zh: 铃响了。我们不得不去上课，但争论像慢性头痛一样跟着我们。在班会上，黑尔老师把我分配到百年纪念委员会，作为对"过度社交突出"的惩罚。我一个字都没说。

paragraphs.en: At lunch, Nora cornered me on the roof. She had a second lunchbox. This one contained rice balls that were slightly burned and a note that said "EAT."
paragraphs.zh: 午餐时，诺拉在屋顶堵住我。她带了第二个便当盒。这个里面是有点烧焦的饭团和一张写着"吃"的纸条。

paragraphs.en: "Promise one starts now," she said. "You have to eat my cooking for a week. Starting with these."
paragraphs.zh: "第一个承诺现在开始,"她说,"你得吃我做的一周饭菜。从这些开始。"

paragraphs.en: I took a bite. The rice was hard in the middle. I chewed carefully. "It's..."
paragraphs.zh: 我咬了一口。米饭中间是硬的。我小心地嚼着。"这..."

paragraphs.en: "Don't say wholesome again," she warned.
paragraphs.zh: "别再说健康了,"她警告道。

paragraphs.en: "It has character," I said.
paragraphs.zh: "很有个性,"我说。

paragraphs.en: She laughed, then her laugh turned into a sigh. "I'm not good at this," she admitted. "But I want to do it. I want to keep the promise. So you have to uphold your end."
paragraphs.zh: 她笑了，然后笑声变成了叹息。"我不擅长这个,"她承认,"但我想做。我想守住承诺。所以你也要遵守你那边。"

paragraphs.en: There was an awkward silence. I could see she was trying to say something else, but the words got tangled. Finally, she just said, "Eat the rice."
paragraphs.zh: 一阵尴尬的沉默。我看得出她想说别的，但话缠住了。最后，她只说:"吃米饭。"

paragraphs.en: After school, I went to the library to read the notebook in peace. But Vivian was already there, sitting at a table with a pile of books and a determined expression.
paragraphs.zh: 放学后，我去图书馆安静地读笔记本。但薇薇安已经在那里了，坐在桌边，面前堆着书，表情坚定。

paragraphs.en: "I've been researching the school's history," she said. "The Memory Club existed eight years ago. It was disbanded. The Annex was closed. There are no records of its members."
paragraphs.zh: "我一直在研究学校的历史,"她说,"记忆俱乐部八年前存在过。后来解散了。附楼关闭了。没有成员的记录。"

paragraphs.en: She slid a photo across the table. It showed a group of children in front of the Annex. I recognized the building, but the faces were blurry. "This is the only photo I could find," she said. "But look closely."
paragraphs.zh: 她把一张照片推过桌子。照片上是一群孩子在附楼前。我认出了那座建筑，但面孔模糊。"这是我唯一能找到的照片,"她说,"但仔细看。"

paragraphs.en: I looked. One of the faces had been scratched out. The scratched-out face was standing next to a boy who looked like me.
paragraphs.zh: 我看了看。其中一张脸被刮掉了。被刮掉的脸站在一个看起来像我的男孩旁边。

paragraphs.en: "That's you, isn't it?" Vivian said. "And the scratched-out face... someone didn't want it seen."
paragraphs.zh: "那是你，对吧?"薇薇安说,"而那张被刮掉的脸...有人不想让它被看到。"

paragraphs.en: I felt a chill. "Who would do that?"
paragraphs.zh: 我感到一阵寒意。"谁会这么做?"

paragraphs.en: "That's what I intend to find out," she said. "But first, we need to talk about the notebook. I want to propose a defense against Nora's cooking. You need someone to appraise the food objectively. I can do that."
paragraphs.zh: "这正是我想弄清楚的,"她说,"但首先，我们需要谈谈笔记本。我想提议一个针对诺拉烹饪的防御措施。你需要有人客观地评估食物。我可以做。"

paragraphs.en: I stared at her. "You want to be my food taster?"
paragraphs.zh: 我瞪着她。"你想当我的食物品尝师?"

paragraphs.en: "I want to ensure the promise is kept with rigour," she said. "And I want to read the notebook. It's part of the school's chronicle."
paragraphs.zh: "我想确保承诺被严格履行,"她说,"而且我想读笔记本。它是学校编年史的一部分。"

paragraphs.en: Before I could answer, Mia appeared at the library door. She walked over and placed a small drawing on the table. It was a sketch of the roof, with two figures eating lunch. One was Nora. One was me.
paragraphs.zh: 我还没来得及回答，米娅出现在图书馆门口。她走过来，把一张小画放在桌上。那是一张屋顶的速写，两个人物在吃午餐。一个是诺拉。一个是我。

paragraphs.en: "I added it to the notebook," Mia said quietly. "Page four. It's not a promise. It's a memory."
paragraphs.zh: "我把它加到笔记本里了,"米娅轻声说,"第四页。它不是承诺。是记忆。"

paragraphs.en: Vivian looked at the drawing, then at Mia. "You have the notebook?"
paragraphs.zh: 薇薇安看看画，又看看米娅。"你有笔记本?"

paragraphs.en: Mia shook her head. "I had it. For eight years. I kept it safe. But now it's Elliot's."
paragraphs.zh: 米娅摇摇头。"我曾经有。八年了。我保管着它。但现在它是埃利奥特的。"

paragraphs.en: The silence was thick. I realized then that the notebook was not just a set of promises. It was a chronicle of something that had happened eight years ago, and each of us was tangled in it.
paragraphs.zh: 沉默浓重。我那时意识到，笔记本不仅仅是一套承诺。它是八年前发生之事的编年史，而我们每个人都纠缠其中。

paragraphs.en: "We should open the seventh page," I said.
paragraphs.zh: "我们应该打开第七页,"我说。

paragraphs.en: Vivian and Mia exchanged a glance. "We can't," Vivian said. "The rules say it stays sealed until the centennial. And we don't know who wrote it. The handwriting is different."
paragraphs.zh: 薇薇安和米娅交换了一个眼神。"我们不能,"薇薇安说,"规则说它要保持密封直到百年纪念。而且我们不知道是谁写的。笔迹不同。"

paragraphs.en: "But why would someone write a promise in my notebook and not sign it?" I asked.
paragraphs.zh: "但为什么会有人在我的笔记本里写承诺却不签名?"我问。

paragraphs.en: Mia looked down. "Maybe they did sign it. Maybe the signature is the clue."
paragraphs.zh: 米娅低下头。"也许他们签了。也许签名就是线索。"

paragraphs.en: That night, I lay in bed and thought about the scratched-out face. I thought about Nora's cooking and Vivian's rules and Mia's drawing. The notebook was a chronic condition now, and I had no idea how to cure it.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，我躺在床上，想着那张被刮掉的脸。我想着诺拉的烹饪、薇薇安的规则、米娅的画。笔记本现在是一种慢性病了，我不知道如何治愈它。

paragraphs.en: My phone buzzed. A message from an unknown number: "You opened it. Now you have to keep them all. But be careful. The seventh promise is not what you think."
paragraphs.zh: 我的手机响了。一条来自未知号码的消息:"你打开了它。现在你必须遵守所有承诺。但要小心。第七个承诺不是你想的那样。"

paragraphs.en: I stared at the message. Then I typed back: "Who are you?"
paragraphs.zh: 我盯着消息。然后打字回复:"你是谁?"

paragraphs.en: No answer. The screen went dark. Outside, the wind rattled my window, and I felt the first drop of rain. The centennial was months away, but it already felt like a threshold I wasn't ready to cross.
paragraphs.zh: 没有回答。屏幕暗了。外面，风敲打着窗户，我感到了第一滴雨。百年纪念还有几个月，但它已经感觉像是一个我还没准备好跨越的门槛。

chapters.title: The Roof, the Rules, and the Rice Balls
chapters.subtitle: 屋顶、规则与饭团

paragraphs.en: The rooftop door was locked, which was my first mistake. My second mistake was thinking I could hide there.
paragraphs.zh: 天台的门锁着，这是我的第一个错误。我的第二个错误是以为我能躲在那里。

paragraphs.en: “El! I know you're up there!” Nora's voice echoed up the stairwell. “You can't escape promise number one!”
paragraphs.zh: “埃尔！我知道你在上面！”诺拉的声音在楼梯间回荡。“你逃不掉第一个约定的！”

paragraphs.en: I pressed my back against the wall and tried to become part of the concrete. It didn't work. Nora appeared at the top of the stairs, her cheeks flushed, holding a lunchbox that looked dangerously heavy.
paragraphs.zh: 我背靠着墙，试图让自己变成混凝土的一部分。但没用。诺拉出现在楼梯口，脸颊通红，手里拿着一个看起来危险地沉重的饭盒。

paragraphs.en: “The roof is off-limits without a teacher,” I said, trying to sound like a rule-follower. “It's a barrier for a reason.”
paragraphs.zh: “没有老师允许，屋顶是禁止进入的，”我说，试图听起来像遵守规则的人。“它设障碍是有原因的。”

paragraphs.en: Nora ignored me and sat down on the top step. “Then we'll eat on the stairs. Come on. I made these myself. With love.”
paragraphs.zh: 诺拉没理我，在最高一级台阶上坐下。“那我们就在楼梯上吃。来吧。我自己做的。用爱做的。”

paragraphs.en: I sat down next to her, because refusing would have been more trouble. She opened the lunchbox. Inside were rice balls. At least, they had started as rice balls. Now they were more like small, burnt rocks with spots of pink.
paragraphs.zh: 我在她旁边坐下，因为拒绝会更麻烦。她打开饭盒。里面是饭团。至少，它们一开始是饭团。现在它们更像烧焦的小石头，上面还有粉色的斑点。

paragraphs.en: “Is that… salmon?” I asked.
paragraphs.zh: “那是……三文鱼吗？”我问。

paragraphs.en: “It's a secret ingredient!” she said, too loudly. “Just eat it. You promised.”
paragraphs.zh: “这是秘密配料！”她太大声地说。“快吃。你答应过的。”

paragraphs.en: I took a bite. It was exceedingly salty and tasted faintly of burnt toast. I chewed. Nora watched me like a physician watching a patient for a reaction.
paragraphs.zh: 我咬了一口。非常咸，还有点烤焦的面包味。我嚼着。诺拉看着我，像医生观察病人的反应一样。

paragraphs.en: “It's… good,” I said, which was an outrageous lie. But the notebook's rules said I had to praise it. And I couldn't lie well.
paragraphs.zh: “挺……好吃的，”我说，这是个离谱的谎言。但笔记本的规则说我必须称赞它。而且我不擅长撒谎。

paragraphs.en: Nora's face lit up. “Really? You're not just saying that?”
paragraphs.zh: 诺拉的脸亮了起来。“真的吗？你不是随便说的？”

paragraphs.en: “I would never,” I said, and took another bite to prove it. The things I do for promises.
paragraphs.zh: “我绝不会，”我说，又咬了一口证明。我为了约定做的事啊。

paragraphs.en: A week of this. Seven consecutive days of Nora's cooking. The notebook was going to kill me.
paragraphs.zh: 这样要持续一周。连续七天吃诺拉做的饭。笔记本会要了我的命。

paragraphs.en: As I chewed, Vivian appeared at the bottom of the stairs. She looked up at us with a cool, amused smile. “Eating on the stairs is a violation of school statute number forty-two,” she said. “But I'll overlook it. I came to discuss supervision.”
paragraphs.zh: 我嚼着的时候，薇薇安出现在楼梯底部。她带着冷静、好笑的微笑抬头看我们。“在楼梯上吃东西违反了学校章程第四十二条，”她说。“但我可以忽略。我来讨论监督的事。”

paragraphs.en: “Supervision?” Nora said, her mouth full.
paragraphs.zh: “监督？”诺拉满嘴食物地说。

paragraphs.en: “Someone has to make sure these promises are carried out properly,” Vivian said. “And since I'm the student council secretary, I'm the natural choice. I propose a supervision committee. Me.”
paragraphs.zh: “得有人确保这些约定被正确执行，”薇薇安说。“既然我是学生会秘书，我自然是合适人选。我提议成立一个监督委员会。就是我。”

paragraphs.en: Nora swallowed and stood up. “You just want to spy on us!”
paragraphs.zh: 诺拉咽下食物，站起来。“你只是想监视我们！”

paragraphs.en: “I want to prevent chaos,” Vivian said. “And I want the notebook for the centennial exhibit. Think about it. A chronicle of childhood promises. It would be a fabulous attraction. A legacy for the town.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想防止混乱，”薇薇安说。“而且我想要那本笔记本用于百年庆典展览。想想吧。童年约定的编年史。会是个极好的吸引力。给小镇的遗产。”

paragraphs.en: “It's not a legacy, it's mine!” Nora said. “Well, ours. But mostly his.”
paragraphs.zh: “这不是遗产，这是我的！”诺拉说。“好吧，我们的。但主要是他的。”

paragraphs.en: “The notebook doesn't belong to anyone yet,” Vivian said. “According to the rules, a promise is only kept when the other person says so. So I'm here to oversee. To make sure no one cheats.”
paragraphs.zh: “笔记本还不属于任何人，”薇薇安说。“根据规则，只有对方说完成，约定才算完成。所以我来监督。确保没人作弊。”

paragraphs.en: I raised a hand. “Can I say something?”
paragraphs.zh: 我举起手。“我能说句话吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No,” they said together.
paragraphs.zh: “不行，”她们异口同声。

paragraphs.en: So that was how the supervision committee began. Vivian would monitor the promises. Nora would cook. And I would eat. The bureaucracy of childhood was alive and well.
paragraphs.zh: 监督委员会就这样开始了。薇薇安监督约定。诺拉做饭。我吃。童年的官僚制度活得好好的。

paragraphs.en: After school, I went to the library to escape. But Mia was there, sitting at a table with her sketchbook. She looked up when I came in and nodded.
paragraphs.zh: 放学后，我去图书馆逃避。但米娅在那里，坐在桌边，拿着速写本。我进来时她抬头点了点头。

paragraphs.en: “Hiding?” she asked.
paragraphs.zh: “躲？”她问。

paragraphs.en: “Maybe,” I said. “Mind if I sit?”
paragraphs.zh: “也许，”我说。“介意我坐吗？”

paragraphs.en: She shook her head. I sat across from her. She was drawing the window, the light, the dust motes. Her hand moved in short, sure strokes.
paragraphs.zh: 她摇摇头。我在她对面坐下。她在画窗户、光线、灰尘。她的手以短促、确定的笔触移动。

paragraphs.en: “I saw the photo,” I said quietly. “The one with the scratched-out face.”
paragraphs.zh: “我看到照片了，”我轻声说。“那张脸被刮掉的照片。”

paragraphs.en: Mia's pencil stopped. She didn't look up. “I know.”
paragraphs.zh: 米娅的铅笔停了。她没有抬头。“我知道。”

paragraphs.en: “Do you know who it was?”
paragraphs.zh: “你知道那是谁吗？”

paragraphs.en: She was silent for a long moment. Then she said, “I have a theory. But I don't like it.”
paragraphs.zh: 她沉默了很久。然后她说：“我有个推测。但我不喜欢它。”

paragraphs.en: Before I could ask more, the library door opened and Theo burst in. “Elliot! There you are! The betting pool is up to fifty! People are betting on whether you'll survive Nora's cooking!”
paragraphs.zh: 我还没来得及多问，图书馆门开了，西奥冲进来。“埃利奥特！你在这儿！赌池已经到五十了！大家在赌你能不能挺过诺拉的厨艺！”

paragraphs.en: Mia closed her sketchbook. “I should go,” she said. “My grandmother needs help at the kiosk.”
paragraphs.zh: 米娅合上速写本。“我该走了，”她说。“我奶奶在报刊亭需要帮忙。”

paragraphs.en: She left before I could say goodbye. Theo flopped into her chair. “She's weird,” he said. “But in a cool way.”
paragraphs.zh: 我还没来得及说再见她就走了。西奥一屁股坐进她的椅子。“她挺奇怪的，”他说。“但酷。”

paragraphs.en: “Did you need something?” I asked.
paragraphs.zh: “你有事吗？”我问。

paragraphs.en: “Yeah. I need advice. There's this girl in class 2-C. She's in the pottery club. I want to ask her out, but I don't know how. You're good with girls, right?”
paragraphs.zh: “有。我需要建议。2-C班有个女孩。她在陶艺社。我想约她出去，但不知道怎么做。你擅长对付女孩，对吧？”

paragraphs.en: I stared at him. “I have three girls fighting over a notebook I don't remember writing. I'm not good with girls. I'm a disaster.”
paragraphs.zh: 我瞪着他。“我有三个女孩为一本我不记得写过的笔记本争吵。我不擅长对付女孩。我是个灾难。”

paragraphs.en: Theo grinned. “Exactly. You're relatable. So, what do I do?”
paragraphs.zh: 西奥咧嘴笑。“正是。你有共鸣。那么，我该怎么做？”

paragraphs.en: I sighed. “Just talk to her. Be honest. Don't start a betting pool.”
paragraphs.zh: 我叹气。“就跟她说话。诚实点。别开赌池。”

paragraphs.en: “Got it. Thanks, man!” He ran off.
paragraphs.zh: “明白了。谢了，兄弟！”他跑开了。

paragraphs.en: I stayed in the library until the sun went down. When I finally left, the sky was orange and the air was cool. I walked past the station. The kiosk was closed, but a light was on inside. Mia was there, wiping the counter.
paragraphs.zh: 我在图书馆待到太阳下山。最后离开时，天空是橙色的，空气凉爽。我经过车站。报刊亭关了，但里面有灯。米娅在那里，擦着柜台。

paragraphs.en: She saw me and waved. I waved back. She pointed at the notebook in my bag, then at herself, then made a drawing motion. I understood: she wanted to add another drawing. I nodded.
paragraphs.zh: 她看到我，挥了挥手。我挥手回应。她指指我包里的笔记本，然后指指自己，做了个画画的动作。我明白了：她想再画一幅。我点头。

paragraphs.en: As I walked home, my phone buzzed. A text from the unknown number again: “The seventh promise is not what you think. The handwriting is not yours. Ask your mother.”
paragraphs.zh: 走回家时，手机震动了。又是那个未知号码的短信：“第七个约定不是你想的那样。笔迹不是你的。问你母亲。”

paragraphs.en: I stopped walking. The sun had set, and the streetlights were flickering on. The words hung in the air like smoke. I didn't want to ask my mother. I was afraid of the answer.
paragraphs.zh: 我停下脚步。太阳已经落山，路灯闪烁亮起。那些话像烟一样悬在空中。我不想问我母亲。我害怕答案。
